references.text: Moses and Aaron were to go together to Pharaoh, which shows their shared mission as leaders of Israel.
Moses and Aaron gathered the elders of Israel, who later met them after the audience with Pharaoh.
Moses and Aaron went in to Pharaoh together, and now they come out again after their request was rejected.
The Israelite overseers were beaten and complained to Pharaoh, which led to their meeting Moses and Aaron.
The overseers accused Moses and Aaron of making them hateful in Pharaoh's eyes, as a direct continuation of this meeting.
Uses the same Hebrew verb פָּגַע (to meet, encounter) in a similar context about meeting someone.
Both verses illustrate the critical transition from confrontation with Pharaoh to prayer to the Lord.
6:27 confirms the role Moses and Aaron play throughout the Exodus, including the meeting with the brothers after the confrontation.
Highlights the recurring pattern where Moses withdraws from Pharaoh to pray to the Lord.
Reinforces the pattern that confrontation with Pharaoh consistently leads to prayer by Moses.
Places the specific event within the broader historical and theological context of the Exodus.
Shows that the leaders' actions, even in crisis meetings, are consistent obedience to God's command.
